anat-breast-regions.intro: Two views of the breast itself: a side view of what lies under the skin, and a close-up of the duct and lobule, which is where the difference between ductal and lobular cancer comes from. Explore each view, then switch to Quiz mode.

plates.title: Breast Side View (Sagittal)
plates.caption: Sagittal section of the breast: nipple on the left, chest wall on the right. Illustration by Patrick J. Lynch, CC BY 2.5.

hotspots.label: Skin
hotspots.blurb: Skin changes stage the tumor: ulceration, satellite nodules, or peau d'orange edema = T4b; inflammatory cancer = T4d.

hotspots.label: Cooper's Ligaments
hotspots.blurb: Fibrous bands from the skin to the chest wall. Tumor pulling on them causes skin dimpling and retraction.

hotspots.label: Glandular Tissue (Lobes)
hotspots.blurb: 15-20 lobes, each draining through its own duct to the nipple. Dense glandular tissue lowers mammogram sensitivity.

hotspots.label: Lactiferous Ducts
hotspots.blurb: Main ducts converging on the nipple. Nipple retraction or bloody discharge can come from a tumor involving these ducts.

hotspots.label: Retromammary Fat
hotspots.blurb: Fat plane between the breast and the pectoralis fascia. Its preservation on imaging suggests no deep invasion.

hotspots.label: Pectoralis Major
hotspots.blurb: Tumor invading only the pectoralis muscle is NOT T4a. Chest wall (T4a) means ribs, intercostal muscles, or serratus anterior.

hotspots.label: Chest Wall (Ribs / Intercostals)
hotspots.blurb: True chest wall invasion = T4a. The chest wall is the target after mastectomy (PMRT).

plates.title: Duct & Lobule (TDLU)
plates.caption: Schematic of a breast lobe from the nipple (top) down to the terminal duct lobular units (circled). Source: Banik U et al., J Exp Clin Cancer Res 2017 (PMC5517797), Fig. 1, CC BY 4.0; labels and pointer lines removed.

hotspots.label: Lobule (Acini)
hotspots.blurb: Milk-producing acini. Lobular carcinoma cells look like lobule cells: small, uniform, and they lose E-cadherin.

hotspots.label: Terminal Duct Lobular Unit
hotspots.blurb: Where almost all breast cancers start, both ductal and lobular. 'Ductal' vs 'lobular' describes how the cells look, not exactly where they start.

hotspots.label: Terminal Duct
hotspots.blurb: Small duct leading out of the lobule into the larger duct system.

hotspots.label: Segmental (Major) Duct
hotspots.blurb: Larger ducts leading to the nipple. DCIS fills and spreads along ducts, which is why it often shows up as linear or branching calcifications.

hotspots.label: Lactiferous Sinus
hotspots.blurb: Dilated segment just under the nipple where milk collects.

hotspots.label: Intralobular Stroma
hotspots.blurb: Loose connective tissue inside and around the lobule. Invasive cancer grows into the stroma: IDC forms a firm, spiculated mass; ILC infiltrates in single-file lines without a clear mass.

gallery.title: Clinical photo: peau d'orange
gallery.caption: Right inflammatory breast cancer: diffuse erythema and peau d'orange skin edema (T4d). Levine PH et al., Cancers 2010 (PMC3827596), CC BY 3.0.

gallery.title: Histology: IDC
gallery.caption: Cohesive nests and glands forming a mass. Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, CC0.

anat-breast-nodes.intro: The regional nodes of the breast are defined by one muscle: the pectoralis minor. Work through the nodal basins first, then the three axillary levels, and make sure you can place each boundary cold.

plates.title: Regional Nodal Basins
plates.caption: Front view of the chest showing lymphatic drainage of the right breast (on your left): toward the axilla, up to the clavicle, and medially along the sternum.

hotspots.label: Axillary Nodes (Levels I-III)
hotspots.blurb: The main drainage for every part of the breast (~75% of lymph). Divided into levels I, II, III by the pectoralis minor.

hotspots.label: Supraclavicular Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Above the clavicle, from the cricoid down to the clavicular head, between the SCM and scalene muscles. Involved SCV nodes = cN3c (Stage IIIC), still curable.

hotspots.label: Internal Mammary Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the internal mammary vessels, just lateral to the sternum in intercostal spaces 1-3. Medial and central tumors drain here.

hotspots.label: Infraclavicular Nodes (Level III)
hotspots.blurb: The highest axillary level, just below the clavicle and medial to the pectoralis minor. Involvement = cN3a.

hotspots.label: Rotter's (Interpectoral) Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Between the pectoralis major and minor, counted with level II.

hotspots.label: Sentinel Node
hotspots.blurb: The first node that drains the tumor, almost always in level I. Sentinel node biopsy replaced routine axillary dissection for a clinically negative axilla.

plates.title: Axillary Levels I-III
plates.caption: Drawing of the right axilla: level I nodes (red) lateral to the pectoralis minor, level II (purple) behind it, level III (blue) medial to it. Source: Lu Q et al., PLoS One 2013 (PMC3702586), Fig. 1, CC BY 4.0; labels and legend removed.

hotspots.label: Level I (Lateral to Pec Minor)
hotspots.blurb: Lateral to the lateral border of the pectoralis minor, down to about the 4th-5th rib. The sentinel node is usually here. Standard 'high tangents' cover much of it.

hotspots.label: Level II (Behind Pec Minor)
hotspots.blurb: Directly behind (deep to) the pectoralis minor, including Rotter's nodes. A standard ALND removes levels I and II.

hotspots.label: Level III (Medial to Pec Minor)
hotspots.blurb: Medial to the medial border of the pectoralis minor, up to the clavicle. Also called infraclavicular. Not routinely dissected, but covered in regional nodal RT.

hotspots.label: Pectoralis Minor
hotspots.blurb: THE landmark: level I is lateral, level II is behind, level III is medial. It runs from ribs 3-5 up to the coracoid process.

hotspots.label: Axillary Vein
hotspots.blurb: Runs through the axilla toward the clavicle. The upper limit of an axillary dissection.

gallery.caption: Left chest wall and regional nodal targets after mastectomy: (a) internal mammary (IMLN), chest wall (CW), and axillary (AXLN) volumes; (b) supraclavicular (SCF) and infraclavicular (ICF) volumes higher up. Pink is the PTV. Yu PC et al., Radiat Oncol 2018 (PMC6260755), Fig. 1a-b, CC BY 4.0.

gallery.caption: Pectoralis major (P Maj) cut and reflected to show the pectoralis minor (P Min) and the axillary fat and nodes (arrowheads). Cocco G et al., Insights Imaging 2023 (PMC10175532), CC BY 4.0.
